titles: Creator name first, then the bet or question in plain verbs, max 6 words. Never put the result in the title; Red Card, Copper and Hang On all gave away the payoff.
Use the question form for the stake ('Asks If This Dog Is Ever Happy') and avoid trivia like 'Japan's Most Popular Dog'.
Use one or two emoji at the end only. Don't stack flags or pairs that don't mean anything.
hooks: Max 6 words and add the stake the narrator didn't. If the hook and narrator say the same thing, cut one.
Cut vague teases like 'WAIT FOR HIS LIFE ADVICE'. State what is on the line or what will break ('LOSE AND THE STREAM ENDS').
Don't write hooks that announce the outcome, like 'ONE HIT AWAY'; ask whether it happens.
clip_picks: Only cut moments with a one-line spoken premise (bet, guess, countdown, question). Speed and Kai with athletes or celebrities come first, then Kai with Ray.
Skip visual-only moments (fans chasing, a clinch, a dog, a boss fight buildup). If the transcript isn't funny read aloud, skip it.
Mine Jynxzi rank guessing as a repeatable series, but state the premise up front.
length_and_pacing: Stop cutting every clip to 53s. Start ≤2s before the stake line, end ≤2s after the payoff, and aim for 15-30s. The breakouts are mostly 11-26s.
End on the payoff line and cut trailing banter so the clip loops cleanly.
posting: Post 1-2 clips a day within hours of the stream. Clips 5-7 days old compete with hundreds of other clippers.
All clips sit at 0-15 views with n/a analytics, so check Studio for limits, duplicate-content flags and Shorts-feed serving before judging. After 48h, judge on 3s retention and Shorts-feed share.
Check that scheduled clips actually went public; four are still private.

money.idea: Join paid clipping campaigns, starting with N3on.
money.why: With 0 subs, YPP is far off (0/500 subs, 20 views against a 3M Shorts-view threshold for fan funding). Campaigns pay per view on the same Speed, Kai and Jynxzi style clips you already cut.
money.first_step: Read the N3on campaign rules for allowed creators, minimum length and payout, then cut one 15-30s clip to spec and submit it.

money.idea: Build a Jynxzi rank-guessing series and package it for a sponsor later.
money.why: A repeatable premise gives viewers a reason to subscribe. A named series is easier to pitch than random clips.
money.first_step: Cut three rank-guess clips from the same stream with the premise stated in the first 2s, and give them a shared title format.

money.idea: Compile a weekly long-form 'best of' per streamer once Shorts get views.
money.why: Long-form earns ad revenue under normal YPP rules without needing Shorts views, but it needs 1000 subs and 4,000 watch hours. It also reuses the clips that already work.
money.first_step: Pick the top 5 clips by 3s retention after 48h and note which ones to stitch into a 5-8 minute compilation.

money.idea: Check the clipped creators' own clipping or affiliate programs.
money.why: Some streamers pay or give codes for clips. Speed, Kai and Adin have large communities, and an approved clipper gets better access.
money.first_step: Look for each creator's clipper or Discord program and send one short message with two sample clips.
